assumptions.description: The split rests on a COST proxy, not on output. The regional structural business statistics publish local units, wages and persons employed at NUTS-2, and neither turnover nor value added, so nothing published measures the three sections' output for Catalonia. S1 uses wages because they track value more closely than a headcount.
assumptions.source: Eurostat, Structural business statistics by NUTS 2 region and NACE Rev. 2 (sbs_r_nuts06_r2), Catalonia, 2018
assumptions.validated_by: MEASURED against the other published indicator: the two disagree most on `I`, 17.4 % by wages against 25.2 % by headcount, 7.9 points apart
assumptions.impact_on_results: up to 7.9 points of the parent's output on one subsector; the report prints both scenarios rather than ranking them

assumptions.description: Every subsector inherits the parent's input structure. With one allocation key the weight cancels in a_ij = Z_ij / X_j, so all three share `G-I`'s multiplier. Differentiating them would need purchasing profiles, and nothing published gives them for a NUTS-2 region.
assumptions.applies_to: the multipliers of G, H and I
assumptions.source: Sizes: Eurostat, Structural business statistics by NUTS 2 region and NACE Rev. 2 (sbs_r_nuts06_r2), Catalonia, 2018 || Structures: NOT ESTIMATED
assumptions.impact_on_results: the three subsectors' multipliers are the parent's and should be quoted as such

assumptions.description: That sections G, H and I tile the archive's `G-I`. `G-I` is Eurostat's A10 grouping, which `check_split` does not parse, so the engine accepts the split and says it could not verify the tiling. The grouping is documented by Eurostat as G, H and I; it is read from there rather than derived here.
assumptions.applies_to: whether the parts add up to the parent
assumptions.validated_by: read from the classification, not measured
assumptions.impact_on_results: none on the arithmetic — the parts are scaled to the parent's own total either way — but a reader who believed the grouping were G and I alone would be reading transport into the wrong row

assumptions.description: The table is an ESTIMATE, cell by cell: the archive is modelled from the OECD ICIO, Eurostat regional accounts and truck freight flows. Neither of its accounting identities closes, and the residue is carried in a labelled RESIDUAL row and column rather than balanced away. Against ten surveyed regions it records about a quarter of the purchases a region makes from the rest of its country, so the share of an impulse that stays in Catalonia is an upper bound.
assumptions.source: Huang, S. & Koutroumpis, P. (2023), European multi regional input output data for 2008-2018, Scientific Data 10, 218
assumptions.impact_on_results: the split is exact arithmetic on estimated cells; the report sizes the residue and states the bound beside the figures
